rv.q: A show that's lush and haunting, even if overlong...tightly choreographed and genuinely inventive.

Here is one of the great lost-love tales of all time. If it falls a little short in this jazz musical, that is because the whole enterprise is a touch too hip for characterisation or humour to flourish. But this is a show with plenty of spectacle...Despite a certain level of nonsense, the show trots along and has a handsome swagger.
The sepulchral funk score is a blissed-out delight, but it can't overcome the show's dramatic shortcomings.

cn.t: Critics praise Hadestown's lush, jazz-infused score and inventive staging, though most find the story thin and dramatically uneven. The show's cool aesthetic and musical feast largely compensate for an overloaded book and slow pace.
